subject: Graduated surcharge mitigation & sunrise protection — Order Form LA-1187
messages:
From: Ava Brooks <ava.brooks@luminateanalytics.com>

Cc: procurement <procurement@luminateanalytics.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed redlines: graduated surcharge & sunrise protection (Order Form #LA-1187)

Ben —

Thanks for the call last week. Our procurement team reviewed the draft order form and we logged two blocking commercial items around the surcharge mechanics that will prevent internal approval unless we get smoother ramp mechanics and a clearer sunset/true-up. I attached a redline (Luminate_Redline_v3.docx) with the edits, but the key asks are below:

- Replace the step-function surcharge that triggers at 500M tokens with a graduated surcharge that phases in over 3 bands (500–750M, 750–1B, >1B) so our monthly bills don’t jump dramatically.
- Add a 90‑day sunrise protection so surcharges only apply after a sustained 2‑month run-rate above the relevant band.
- Cap the incremental surcharge at 12% of baseline spend in any billing month (our internal limit).

We appreciate Redwood’s position on ensuring economic protections, but a smoothing mechanism + short sunset will let us pilot with predictable economics. Can your team review and propose alternate contract language or commercial offsets (e.g., temporary larger floor, initial discount taper) to close this?

We’re aiming to finish commercial terms this week — can we do a 30‑minute call tomorrow afternoon?

Thanks,
Ava Brooks
Head of Procurement
Luminate Analytics

Attachments: Luminate_Redline_v3.docx (docx), Pricing_Summary_Q42026.xlsx (xlsx)

Ava — thanks for the clear summary and for the redline. I’ve reviewed the high‑level asks and agree they’re reasonable to discuss.

Quick notes:
- We can propose a graduated surcharge structure rather than a hard step; commercial would prefer a 2‑band approach to keep complexity down, but I’ll include a 3‑band option for flexibility.
- Sunrise / run‑rate protections are also negotiable — legal will want specific trigger language (e.g., 2 consecutive months above band) which matches what you proposed.
- The cap at 12% is tight but not impossible if we balance via an elevated floor for the first 6 months or an initial pilot discount.

Looping in Marissa (lead for enterprise deals) and Lauren (pricing ops) to scope tradeoffs and draft suggested language. Marissa / Lauren — can you review the attached redline and propose 1) working language for a graduated surcharge clause (3 bands + run-rate trigger), and 2) a short commercial concession we can offer (e.g., 6‑month reduced floor or first‑quarter rebate) that keeps our downside reasonable?

Ava — can you do a 30‑minute sync tomorrow at 2pm PT? I’ll send a calendar invite if that works.

Best,
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Ben / Lauren —

Thanks — read through Ava’s redline. Below are suggested commercial/legal-first‑pass items I can support to unblock approvals quickly. I’ve pasted proposed language we can send to Luminate as an alternative redline.

Proposed commercial package (two options):
Option A (conservative, faster legal acceptance):
- Convert surcharge to two bands: 500–800M tokens (3% incremental), >800M tokens (6% incremental).
- 60‑day sustained run‑rate trigger (two consecutive billing cycles).
- Monthly surcharge capped at 12% of baseline invoice.
- 6‑month elevated floor (5% lower than baseline) in months 1–6 as a customer-friendly ramp.

Option B (more Luminate‑friendly):
- Three bands: 500–700M (2%), 700–900M (4%), >900M (6%).
- 90‑day run‑rate trigger.
- Cap at 12%.
- 3‑month initial rebate equal to 50% of surcharge in months 1–3 after trigger.

Draft working clause (for inclusion in Exhibit B — Pricing Schedule):
"Graduated Surcharge. In the event Customer’s monthly token consumption exceeds the thresholds set forth in the Pricing Schedule, Redwood will apply a graduated surcharge as follows: Band 1 (500–700,000,000 tokens): 2% surcharge; Band 2 (700–900,000,000 tokens): 4% surcharge; Band 3 (>900,000,000 tokens): 6% surcharge. Surcharges shall only be applied after Customer has exceeded the applicable band in two (2) consecutive billing cycles (the "Run‑Rate Trigger"). In no event shall incremental surcharges in a single billing cycle exceed 12% of the Baseline Invoice Amount. The Parties may agree to a temporary rebate or elevated floor during the initial months following a Run‑Rate Trigger as described in the Pricing Schedule."

Ask: Ben — please confirm which option you want to present (A or B) and whether we should offer the rebate (Option B) or the elevated floor (Option A) as the primary commercial concession. I can then finalize redline text and legal will run for a quick approval.

-Marissa
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Thanks — Option B (three bands + 90‑day trigger + short rebate) is closest to our internal risk tolerance. The rebate path is acceptable to our finance team instead of an elevated floor. A couple of clarifications we need in any revised clause:
- Define Baseline Invoice Amount (we expect this to be the average of prior 3 billing cycles).
- Rebate mechanics: if a surcharge is charged, the rebate should be applied on the subsequent invoice within the same quarter.
- Add audit rights to confirm token counts and ensure no double‑counting across API keys.

We’re available for the call tomorrow at 2pm PT. If you can send the revised redline before the call, our legal can pre‑review.

Ava

Subject: Final working language + next steps — LA‑1187

Ava —

Great working session today. Per our discussion, attached is the revised Exhibit B wording implementing Option B with the clarified Baseline definition and rebate mechanics. Key points we committed to: 

- Three bands (500–700M / 700–900M / >900M) with rates 2% / 4% / 6%.
- Run‑rate Trigger: two consecutive billing cycles above the threshold; surcharge applies beginning with the billing cycle following trigger.
- Baseline Invoice Amount: the average of the three most recent fully completed billing cycles prior to the Run‑Rate Trigger.
- Rebate: any surcharge charged will be credited back at 50% on the subsequent invoice within the same quarter; credits applied within 45 days.
- Audit: Redwood will provide token usage reports and Customer may request a one‑time reconciliation audit per 12 months.
- Monthly surcharge cap: 12% of Baseline Invoice Amount.

Next steps:
1) We’ll upload the final redline to DocuSign for signature: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/LA-1187-sign
2) I’ve attached the updated redline (Final_Redline_LA1187.docx) to the HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/DEAL-2026-1187
3) Legal will prepare the Order Form and we’ll route for countersignature.

If that all looks good I’ll send the DocuSign packet this afternoon. Thanks for working through the details — excited to get Luminate onboarded.

Best,
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
